name: False Cause
shortDef: Assuming that because two things go together, one causes the other.
definition: Concluding that one thing causes another just because they occur or trend together, without ruling out coincidence, reverse causation or a third factor driving both.
howToSpot: Could a third factor be driving both things?
Could the cause run the other way around?
Is there evidence beyond the two things moving together?
classicExample: Towns with more coffee shops have higher incomes, so opening coffee shops will make a town richer.
legitimateVersion: A causal claim is reasonable when an experiment or careful comparison rules out obvious third factors, or when a plausible mechanism is backed by evidence.

contrast.fal_post_hoc: False cause infers causation from things occurring together; post hoc infers it from one event simply coming before another.
contrast.fal_texas_sharpshooter: False cause reads causation into a correlation; the Texas sharpshooter picks a pattern out of random data after the fact.
